patch_description:
The validation output contains no Python traceback, but the original implementation has several correctness failures likely triggered by mixed real-world data: it mutates and merges working frames, writes completed futures back using completion order rather than source-row identity, accesses tuple values through unsafe column-name attributes, can lose valid row/column mappings during recursion, and finally calls `sort_values` across mixed-type columns. It also returns an empty column-ordering list despite permuting values.

This replacement preserves every input cell, row, column, and row identity. It builds bounded candidate column arrangements using normalized serialization only for scoring, evaluates candidates with the exact sorted-string LCP Trie objective, supports row-specific conditional orders, returns valid per-row column orderings, and avoids mixed-type dataframe sorting.
